pairs.difference: A cart: light comes from upper left, the awning scallops throw a dark soft band on the posts and glass, and the cart body turns into a darker right end with contact darkening under the wheels. B helmet: the white shell turns slowly and evenly with no clear core shadow, the only strong dark is the visor reflection, and the floor shadow sits as a detached pool to the right. B's shading_range of 0.596 is below the real 0.658 minimum.
pairs.fix: Light the helmet from the upper left with one strong key. Let the right side of the white shell fall into a clear cool shadow with a visible core band, and tuck a dark contact shadow tightly under the neck ring.

pairs.difference: A topiary: each tier has a bright upper left and a deep dark underside, and a firm cast shadow falls right across the grass, so the key is unmistakable. B planet: a gentle airbrushed gradient runs from a soft top-left sheen to a mild lower-right falloff. The ring casts only a faint band on the sphere, and the small moons are shaded with the same soft ball recipe.
pairs.fix: Hit the planet with a hard side light. Leave a third of the sphere in deep shadow with a defined terminator, and have the ring throw a crisp dark shadow across the bands.

pairs.difference: A case: broad satin shading with a soft falloff on the lower right edge and a quiet cast shadow on the background; bias is low (0.15) but within range. B UFO: sharp white streaks on the dome and hull, a thin bright rim on the dome, and a pale halo around the saucer in the lens, where the background brightens instead of receiving shadow. The underside is dark, but the hot spots read as stuck on.
pairs.fix: Replace the sharp white streaks on the dome and hull with one broad soft sheen. Remove the bright glow around the saucer and let the hull underside fade smoothly into shadow.

pairs.difference: A submarine: the yellow hull turns from a broad top sheen into a deep orange core at the belly and rear, with a soft dark terminator. B rocket: the body is lit from the left with a long white plastic streak and mid-grey on the right, but the fins and nose shade evenly with little core and no shadow from the fins onto the body. Both measure in range, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Soften the white streak on the rocket body into a wide sheen. Cast a dark shadow from the centre fin and the porthole rim onto the hull, and deepen the right side.

pairs.difference: A telescope: side light with a clear shadow underside on the tube and a long, firm, well-placed cast shadow from the tripod across the deck. B ship wheel: frontal light, so the rim and spokes keep nearly one value with only soft edge darkening. A small glow pool on the floor replaces a true cast shadow, and the wheel throws no shadow on its post. Shading_range is 0.573, below the real 0.658 minimum.
pairs.fix: Move the light to the upper left. Have the wheel rim cast a dark shadow on the spokes and post, let the spokes darken on their lower right sides, and lay a long directional shadow across the deck.

pairs.difference: A robot: nearly even frontal grey on the head and torso with soft pillow edges, and little separation between the lit and shadow planes. The long cast shadow to the left is pale and looks detached from the feet. B vending machine: a real plane change, with a bright front face and a left side falling into deep blue, matching the real monitor's lit front and dark side. A's bias of 0.196 sits just under the real floor.
pairs.fix: Light the robot from one upper side so the head and torso have a bright face and a clearly darker side plane. Add dark contact shadows under the feet and joints, and connect the cast shadow to the feet.

pairs.difference: A lion: soft marble form with gentle shadows under the mane and between the plinth steps; form_contrast 0.331 is below range. B envelope: thin soft drop shadows behind paper layers with almost no directional falloff; bias 0.114 is below range. Each misses on a different measure and neither shows a clear lighting tell.

A spyglass: a hard side light, cool blue rim along the top edge, and barrel segments falling to near black below; its bias and contrast exceed the real range, but the brown barrel leaks into the lens. B ray gun: chrome rings and the red body carry crisp hot spots, while a pale halo surrounds the gun in the lens and the body turns evenly with a mild core.
pairs.fix: Remove the pale glow around the gun and darken the underside of the red body with a deep soft core shadow. Reduce the chrome and plastic highlights to fewer, broader shapes.

pairs.difference: A control panel: soft top lighting, with the top deck and buttons shaded almost evenly. There is a darker right side and a soft floor shadow, and the blue floor lights barely affect nearby surfaces. Shading_range is 0.639, below the real 0.658 minimum. B fruit plate: stronger value spread, with shadow under the plate and fruit stacked with clear contact darkening.
pairs.fix: Rake a strong key across the panel from the upper left so the buttons and sliders each cast short dark shadows on the deck. Deepen the right side, and let the blue floor lights tint the panel's lower edge.

pairs.difference: A flower bed: stones and petals have a lit top and a dark lower side with contact shadow under the ring, despite glossy bead highlights. B Ferris wheel: frontal flat light, so cream spokes and rim keep one value along their length, with almost no core shadow and no spoke shadows on the rear structure. Bias is 0.037, far below the real 0.199 floor.
pairs.fix: Light the wheel from one side so each spoke has a bright edge and a dark edge. Let the front rim cast shadows on the rear rim and the cabins, and shade the cabins' lower halves.

pairs.difference: A gate: strong sunlight from the left, with brick piers split into a lit face and a shaded side, firm cast shadows on the paving and a dark contact at the bases. B space station: hazy frontal soft light, with the sphere, tube and solar panels all at similar mid values. It has no terminator, and the docking tube and panels cast no shadow on the hull. Shading_range is 0.588, below the real 0.602 minimum.
pairs.fix: Light the station with a single hard sun from one side. Leave the far side of the sphere in deep shadow, and have the tube and panel arms cast crisp dark shadows on the hull.

pairs.difference: A boat: side light gives clear plane changes on the planks and hull, the dock casts a dark soft shadow, and the boat's shadow sits tight in the water. B pod: an airbrushed ball gradient from a pale left to a dark right. The door lamps and ceiling and floor glow rings do not light the metal around them, so the practicals sit on the surface and the shading ignores them.
pairs.fix: Have the ring lamps throw warm pools of light on the metal around them and the floor ring light the lower hull from below. Darken the hull under the door rim with a tight shadow.

pattern: Generated cards light the hero from the front with a soft wrap-around, so forms turn as even airbrushed gradients, and the shadow side stays shallow with no firm terminator. Real cards commit to one key, with a deep, often cool shadow plane and a clear lit/dark split between planes. Generated parts rarely cast shadows on each other, floor shadows sit detached or get replaced by a glow pool, a pale halo surrounds the hero, sharp white highlights look stuck on, and depicted lights don't illuminate the surfaces around them.
